start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:make-one-piece-of-content-from-audience-to-publish." Make one piece of content (a video, a talk, a carousel, a post or an article) the way a careful studio would, in this order and never skipping ahead to the edit: read the person's own records, their purpose record first; describe any library row that has no crossing fields yet; find what the audience is really asking, in their own words and with where they said it, and whether they would want this; cross ALL of the person's technique, principle and format rows with that goal to get cited ideas; find what the person has already said or written that answers it; choose a format by that material and by measured references; write packages (title, cover, opening) with at least 3 hook variants to test against each other, and show them to people from the audience before making anything; build the script from those filmed points first; check every word against the person's rules and verdicts; write a shoot sheet for only what is still missing; after the person films, grade the sound, colour and cut the piece through the Workshop's tools; run every check before the person sees anything; publish; and read the numbers back to learn.
no_lists_because: The item names no list in its own words, input or steps, so it has no example rows to ship.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Run workflow:make-one-piece-of-content-from-audience-to-publish" with the input in the worked example.

2. The AI starts it with tool:start-a-recipe-run (row workflow:make-one-piece-of-content-from-audience-to-publish) and works through its steps in order: read-records, describe-library, audience, idea, filmed-points, format, titles-and-hooks, pretest, script, check-words, shoot-sheet, film, sound, edit, checks, person-sees, publish, learn.
3. Read what each step hands back; the last step is learn.
